$comment: Example deny-rules for a Microwave-governed repo, Claude Code settings format (translate for other harnesses). READ BEFORE TRUSTING: these cover the Read and Write TOOLS only. They do NOT cover the shell, so a determined agent can still read a file via `cat`, `python -c`, and so on. They are advisory unless your harness actually enforces them. Treat this as a hint that keeps an honest agent on-path, NOT a sandbox and NOT secret protection. The real protection for a secret is to keep it out of the repo entirely (env vars, a secret manager). Copy into .claude/settings.json of the governed repo and adapt paths.

$why: wiki/agents, wiki/adr and INDEX.md are written only by gates/activate.py and the promote paths a human runs: agents draft in wiki/_staging/ and go through the factory flow.
gates/, hooks/, CODEOWNERS and CI definitions are the protected space: changed only via flows/amend-rule.md (PR + gatekeeper).

the two Bash(cat .env*) rules are a token gesture against the most trivial secret read; they are NOT complete (the shell has many other ways), which is exactly why secrets must not live in the repo and why floor 3 (branch protection) is the fence that actually holds.
